def max_fleet_profit(k, gigs):
    """Maximum total pay achievable by a fleet of k identical food trucks.

    You run k food trucks (1 <= k <= 3).  gigs is a non-empty list of at
    most 200 catering gigs; each gig is a tuple (s, e, p) of ints with
    0 <= s < e <= 10**9 and 1 <= p <= 10**6, meaning the gig occupies the
    half-open time interval [s, e) and pays p.

    You may accept any subset of the gigs.  Each accepted gig must be
    assigned to exactly one truck, and the gigs assigned to a single
    truck must be pairwise disjoint as half-open intervals: a truck may
    work a gig ending at time t and another gig starting at that same
    time t, but two gigs whose intervals share an interior point cannot
    go on the same truck.  Unaccepted gigs pay nothing.  Identical
    tuples may appear several times in gigs and count as separate gigs.

    Return the maximum total pay over all valid choices, as an int.

    Bounds: 1 <= len(gigs) <= 200, 1 <= k <= 3.  An exact polynomial
    algorithm is required; trying all assignments is far too slow, and
    repeatedly extracting a maximum-pay schedule for one truck at a time
    is not optimal (the third example below is a counterexample).

    >>> max_fleet_profit(1, [(0, 3, 5), (2, 5, 6), (4, 7, 5)])
    10
    >>> max_fleet_profit(2, [(0, 3, 5), (2, 5, 6), (4, 7, 5)])
    16
    >>> max_fleet_profit(2, [(0, 4, 4), (4, 8, 3), (1, 5, 3), (5, 9, 4)])
    14
    """
